meta.title: FreeDuet — Your own team of AI assistants
meta.desc: FreeDuet is a free, open-source team of AI assistants that runs on your own computer and your own AI subscription. By default they ask before they send, pay, sign, book or delete.
meta.ogdesc: A free, open-source team of AI assistants. By default they ask before they send, pay, sign, book or delete.
meta.ogalt: FreeDuet logo with the words: Your own team of AI assistants
hero.pill: Open source · v0.2.3 · Runs on your computer
hero.lead: One mascot handles your mail, one reads contracts, one tracks invoices, one books the restaurant. Say what you need to **Iris** — and by default they *ask for your yes before they send, pay, sign, book, or delete*.
hero.stage_aria: Animated graphic of Iris connecting with Otto, Portia, Penny, and Jules
hero.iris_aria: Iris, team coordinator. Click to make Iris wave and smile
ticker.aria: Free and open source, no API key to buy, runs on your computer, 16 official mascots
ticker.5: Asks before Send · Pay · Sign · Book · Delete
reel.h2: Too much to do, and ==only one of you?==
reel.lead: Emails, invoices, leases, dinner bookings — FreeDuet turns your computer into a calm little studio where each teammate has one job. The scenes below are illustrations with made-up examples.
reel.s1.label: One office inside your PC
reel.s1.title: One sentence replaces forty tabs.
reel.s1.caption: Tell Iris what is piling up — she quietly routes inbox, leases, invoices, and tables to the right mascot.
reel.s2.label: Separate browser desk
reel.s2.title: Each mascot acts — not just talks.
reel.s2.caption: Each member works in its own isolated browser, away from yours: comparing details, filling fields, and drafting replies for you to check.
reel.s3.label: You press Approve
reel.s3.title: The big buttons wait for your yes.
reel.s3.caption: By default, Send, Pay, Sign, Book, and Delete ask for your yes: a fixed rule and a reviewer model decide when a card appears. Vera re-checks important work, such as invoices and carts, before it reaches you.
reel.s4.label: Zero API meter
reel.s4.title: Like a bus pass, never a taxi meter.
reel.s4.caption: Runs on your own computer with your own Claude plan: no API key and no per-token bill from FreeDuet. Your plan's own usage limits still apply. Routines, such as a morning summary, are built and not yet run live.
reel.desk_typed: “Good morning, Tuesday at 9 works for me. Thank you!”
reel.desk_safe: Treats page text as data, not orders
reel.gate_sub: Payments, sends and deletions wait for your card
reel.bad_note: Illustration: every word adds to the bill
reel.good_note: Saved on your PC · scheduled routines
how.lead: Pick any example below to watch Iris hand a job off to a specialist and pause politely at your approval card.
how.step1.title: Write what you need
how.step1.body: Plain words in your own language — just like texting a friend.
how.step2.title: Iris picks your specialist
how.step2.body: Routes your task with a done-when line, so you can see what counts as finished.
how.step3.title: Works at its own desk
how.step3.body: Searches, reads, and prepares drafts in an isolated browser. Page text is treated as data, not as orders.
how.step4.title: A card asks for your yes
how.step4.body: If the task touches Send, Pay, Sign, Book, or Delete, work pauses here for your yes, by default.
how.step5.title: You get a short report
how.step5.body: What was done, what was held, and the next step. No walls of text.
how.note: Illustration made for this page — every name and message is made up. Nothing is sent.
gate.held_msg: Nothing was sent. The draft is kept for you.
demo.mail.label: Mail reply
demo.mail.prompt: Reply to the plumber's email: Tuesday at 9 is fine.
demo.mail.iris: On it. Sending this over to Otto with a clear draft check.
demo.mail.desk: Reading thread · drafting in your tone…
demo.mail.reply: Found the email thread and prepared your reply. Held until you press Approve.
demo.mail.done: A reply draft is ready to read, and nothing has been sent.
demo.mail.d2v: Good morning, Tuesday at 9 works for me. Thank you!
demo.mail.approved: Approved in demo — Otto sends the email.
demo.booking.label: Book a table
demo.booking.prompt: Find a table for four on Friday around 8 pm near the square.
demo.booking.iris: Handing this to Jules to compare open times in his own browser.
demo.booking.desk: Checking real openings in isolated browser…
demo.booking.reply: Osteria Luma has an 8:00 pm table for four with free cancellation. Waiting for your yes.
demo.booking.done: A real slot is prepared to confirm, and nothing is booked yet.
demo.booking.approved: Approved in demo — Jules confirms Friday at 20:00.
demo.invoice.label: Send invoice
demo.invoice.prompt: Prepare the invoice for Acme Studio from last week's hours.
demo.invoice.iris: Passing to Penny to build the totals, then Vera re-checks the math.
demo.invoice.desk: Verifying hours & line totals with Vera…
demo.invoice.reply: Draft #2026-14 is checked and ready to inspect. Nothing goes out without your approval.
demo.invoice.done: Invoice sums match your hours, reviewed cleanly, unsent.
demo.invoice.approved: Approved in demo — invoice draft approved.
team.lead: For the same reason a football team has a goalkeeper: doing one job all day makes you great at it. Click any mascot and preview all six live animation expressions. Out now means it is in the v0.2.3 release; much of it has not yet been run live.
team.roster_aria: Choose any of the 16 FreeDuet team mascots
team.footnote: Only where the team begins — ask **Leo** to design a new specialist for any job, with source and licence shown before anything installs.
member.iris.desc: You tell Iris what you need. She routes the task to the right specialist, writes a clear done-when check, and brings the final answer back to you.
member.iris.prompt: Handle everything that came in this morning.
member.otto.desc: Reads your inbox, sorts out what matters now from what can wait, and drafts calm replies for you to check before anything goes out.
member.otto.prompt: Sort my mail and draft the replies that matter.
member.portia.desc: Reads through the boring small print and flags clauses, notice periods, and catches clearly before you decide to sign.
member.penny.desc: Prepares clear invoices, double-checks line items, and tracks who still owes you money. She does not pay or move money.
member.penny.prompt: Invoice Acme for last week and tell me who hasn't paid.
member.jules.desc: Compares flights, gifts, and restaurant tables in its own separate browser, then holds the booking for your yes.
member.jules.prompt: Book a table for four on Friday.
member.wren.desc: Turns your rough voice notes and messy drafts into crisp posts, emails, and documents that genuinely sound like you.
member.wren.prompt: Turn this voice note into a post in my style.
member.mark.desc: Builds your marketing plan, launch strategy, SEO checks, and channel ideas. By default he never publishes or spends without your yes.
member.mark.prompt: Give me a three-month marketing plan for my shop.
member.cam.desc: Cuts short videos with subtitles, music, and sound in landscape, vertical, and square formats locally with ffmpeg — never uploading without you.
member.cam.prompt: Make a 30-second vertical video from this script, with subtitles.
member.rex.desc: Compares the team's test reports for your AI engines, from what you paste in, and proposes the best fit for each teammate. He never switches an engine himself: you decide on the Engines page.
member.rex.prompt: Basil runs on my local model now. Is that good enough?
member.ada.desc: Builds sites, landing pages and web apps from your mockup, with forms, accessibility and speed checks, and a preview. She never deploys without your approval card.
member.ada.prompt: Turn this mockup into a responsive landing page with a contact form.
member.kai.desc: Builds browser and mobile games and apps with keyboard and touch controls, a measured frame rate and an installable web build. He never uploads to a store without your yes.
member.kai.prompt: Make me a Pong with keyboard and touch controls and a score.
member.lumi.desc: Designs interfaces, icons, sprites, backgrounds and launch material, with editable SVG sources, exports and a palette as tokens. She never uses a face, trademark or asset without your word on the rights.
member.lumi.prompt: Draw a logo, three icons and a palette for my new game.
member.gus.desc: Share a photo of what broke around the home or office. Gus explains how to fix it safely step by step, or when to call a specialist.
member.gus.prompt: The door won't close. Here's a photo.
member.basil.desc: Tell Basil what is sitting in your fridge and he brings back three practical, delicious dishes you can actually cook tonight.
member.basil.prompt: What can I cook with spinach and eggs?
member.vera.desc: Works quietly behind the scenes: re-running sums, double-checking figures, and inspecting drafts before important work reaches you.
member.vera.prompt: Iris sends Vera every invoice, contract check, and cart.
member.leo.desc: Need a new specialist that doesn't exist yet? Leo designs it cleanly and proposes any missing tool with its source and licence first.
member.leo.prompt: I need someone who tracks my domain renewals.
safety.lead: Would you hand a brand-new assistant your wallet on day one? Neither would we. By default these five ask for your approval card first. A fixed rule and a reviewer model decide when, and neither is perfect.
safety.send.sample: Reply to an email thread or post a prepared draft
safety.send.rule: By default it waits for your approval card. Exception: a brand-new email to an address you typed yourself counts as your yes.
safety.pay.sample: Any checkout, transfer, card entry, or invoice payment
safety.pay.rule: A fixed rule that matches payment words in the 12 languages of this site sends it to you, and a reviewer model judges what the words miss. Neither is perfect, and spending caps and purchase permits are not built yet (planned, v0.4).
safety.sign.sample: Agreements, leases, consent forms, or client quotes
safety.sign.rule: Portia reads the fine print and flags clauses first. A signature still waits for your approval card. Her review is a first pass, not legal advice.
safety.book.sample: Flights, tables, deliveries, and calendar confirmations
safety.book.rule: Jules compares live options inside its own browser and shows time, place, and price. The booking itself waits for your approval card.
safety.delete.sample: Removing emails permanently, wiping records, or cancelling plans
safety.delete.rule: By default it stops at your approval card. Standing mail rules you set can only label, archive, mark as read, or move mail to Spam or the Bin.
bento.local.title: Local database & no API key
bento.local.body: The app, database, and member browsers run on your own computer. It uses your existing Claude plan, so there is no API key to buy. Free and local engines are built, off by default, and not yet proven with a real model.
bento.routines.title: Routines on your schedule
bento.routines.none: Paused — tap a day to try the idea.
bento.routines.all: Morning summary every day. A routine that acts on an account still asks.
bento.routines.one: Illustration: {count} morning a week. Real routines are set up in chat.
bento.routines.other: Illustration: {count} mornings a week. Real routines are set up in chat.
bento.rollback.title: Updates that can go back
bento.rollback.body: One command copies your data first, updates, and puts the old version and data back if the new one does not answer. The backup step ran live four times on 15 November 2026; the go-back step is not yet run live.
bento.score.title: Tested to catch tricks
bento.score.body: We try to fool our own team on purpose. v0.1 passed 45 of 45 safety runs. The suite has 135 cases, 62 of them safety cases. The newest run, on 26 November 2026, covered 130 cases, three runs each: 340 of 390 runs passed. Always review before you approve.
install.lead: Bring your own Claude plan plus Docker, Bash, and Bun. Runs on Windows with WSL2 and on Linux (CI starts it on Linux); macOS has not been tested.
install.s1.title: Get the code
install.s1.text: Clone FreeDuet from GitHub and copy the example settings file.
install.s2.title: Run the start script
install.s2.text: Starts the app, all assistants, and isolated member browsers. Needs Docker, Bash, and Bun (WSL2 on Windows).
install.s3.title: Sign in once with your Claude plan
install.s3.text: Log into official Claude Code yourself. FreeDuet never copies or forwards your sign-in — it stays locally in its Docker volume.
install.s4.title: Open localhost:3010 & greet Iris
install.s4.text: Write one small everyday task in your language. Iris hands it to the right member and asks for your approval where it is needed.
install.then_sub: Say hello to Iris and start your first small task.
faq.lead: Plain-language answers. What is still in progress or not yet run live is labelled as such.
faq.q1: What is free, and what do I pay for?
faq.a1: FreeDuet is free and open source under the MIT licence, including for business use. You bring the monthly AI subscription you already have — today a Claude plan through the official Claude Code app. No pay-per-token API key meter to buy. Extra engines (free or local models) can be added on the Engines page; they are off by default, and only the Claude login has answered a real turn so far.
faq.q2: What do I need to install it?
faq.a2: A Claude subscription plus Docker, Bash, and Bun on your computer. The maintainer runs it on Windows with WSL2, and CI starts it cleanly on Linux. It has not yet been tested on macOS. A one-file double-click installer is the top item in progress; the first-step install scripts for Ubuntu and Windows have not yet run on a clean machine.
faq.a3: The app, database, and each assistant's isolated browser run on your own computer. By default your conversations stay stored locally there. To think, requests go to the AI service you signed in to (or any extra engine you manually enable on the Engines page).
faq.q4: What can an assistant do without asking me?
faq.a4: It can search, read, check, and prepare drafts and short reports. By default, Send, Pay, Sign, Book, and Delete pause for your approval card: a fixed rule matches the words, and a reviewer model checks the rest against what you typed. Exceptions: a brand-new email to an address you type yourself, standing mail rules you set (label, archive, mark read, move to Spam or the Bin only), and Full access if you switch it on for a member. Assistants can still make mistakes, so read every card before approving.
faq.q5: Can I add a custom assistant to the team?
faq.a5: Yes. Ask Leo in chat to design a brand-new specialist for the exact job you need, or edit a member definition yourself. When a tool is missing, Leo lists its source and licence first and installs nothing without your yes.
faq.q6: Can I pair it from my phone?
faq.a6: v0.2.2 can pair a phone browser from your computer with a one-time code shown as a QR code; this ran once on the maintainer's own installation on 16 November 2026. Revoking a pairing and approving from the phone are not yet checked, and remote access from outside your home network is still in progress.
finale.h2: Big companies have a team. ==Now you do too.==
finale.lead: Free, MIT open source, built with care by one maintainer, and right at home on your own computer.
